comparisons.peer_topic: Minimum CET1 Capital Ratio Requirements and Buffers
comparisons.peer_summary: To avoid restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments, the Corporation must meet CET1 capital ratio requirements including buffers and G-SIB surcharges, requiring minimum ratios of 10.0% from Jan 1 to Sep 30, 2024, and 10.7% (Standardized) or 10.0% (Advanced) from Oct 1, 2024. These requirements must be comprised solely of CET1 capital.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America disclose that the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB) is a component of their minimum CET1 capital ratio requirements, specifically applying only to the Standardized approach. GS states the FRB determines the SCB based on its own stress test calculation involving the difference between starting and minimum projected CET1 ratios under the supervisory severely adverse scenario and planned dividends. BAC similarly identifies the SCB as part of the requirements to avoid restrictions on capital distributions, noting it applies only under the Standardized approach (unlike the Advanced approach where it is not included). While GS focuses on the calculation mechanics and BAC focuses on the resulting threshold requirements (10.0% to 10.7%), both confirm the SCB's role in binding capital constraints for the Standardized approach.

sentences.text: The FRB determines the SCB applicable to us based on its own annual stress test.

The SCB under the Standardized approach is calculated as (i) the difference between our starting and minimum projected CET1 capital ratios under the supervisory severely adverse scenario and (ii) our planned common stock dividends for each of the fourth through seventh quarters of the planning horizon, expressed as a percentage of RWAs.

In order to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers, the Corporation must meet risk-based capital ratio requirements that include a capital conservation buffer of 2.5 percent (under the Advanced approaches only), an SCB (under the Standardized approach only), plus any applicable countercyclical capital buffer and a global systemically important bank (G-SIB) surcharge.

For the period from January 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024, the Corporation's minimum CET1 capital ratio requirements were 10.0 percent under both the Standardized approach and the Advanced approaches.

comparisons.peer_topic: Stress Capital Buffer (SCB) Determination and Mechanics
comparisons.peer_summary: The SCB applies to Standardized Approach risk-based capital requirements, replacing the CET1 capital conservation buffer, and is calculated as the greater of the maximum decline in the Common Equity Tier 1 ratio under the severely adverse scenario (adjusted for planned dividends and projected RWAs) or 2.5%, with discretion for the Federal Reserve to recalculate the SCB outside the annual cycle or impose capital action restrictions.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley disclose that the SCB applies only to Standardized Approach requirements and replaces the CET1 capital conservation buffer. GS details the calculation as the difference between starting and minimum projected CET1 ratios under the supervisory severely adverse scenario plus planned dividends. MS provides a more granular formula, stating the SCB is the greater of the maximum decline in CET1 under the severely adverse scenario (adjusted for planned dividends and projected RWAs) or 2.5%. Both firms confirm the FRB determines the SCB annually through supervisory stress testing, and both emphasize the buffer's application is exclusive to the Standardized approach.

The SCB under the Standardized approach is calculated as (i) the difference between our starting and minimum projected CET1 capital ratios under the supervisory severely adverse scenario and (ii) our planned common stock dividends for each of the fourth through seventh quarters of the planning horizon, expressed as a percentage of RWAs.
As part of its annual capital supervisory stress testing process, the Federal Reserve determines an SCB for each large BHC, including us.
The SCB applies only with respect to Standardized Approach risk-based capital requirements and replaced the CET1 capital conservation buffer of 2.5%.

The SCB is the greater of (i) the maximum decline in our Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio under the severely adverse scenario over the supervisory stress test measurement period plus the sum of the four quarters of planned common stock dividends divided by the projected RWAs from the quarter in which the Firm's projected Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio reaches its minimum in the supervisory stress test and (ii) 2.5%.
